questions.label: Which ceremony is this outfit for?

options.label: Nikah
options.description: The Islamic marriage ceremony.

options.label: Mehndi
options.description: The henna celebration before the wedding.

options.label: Baraat
options.description: The main wedding day, welcoming the groom's procession.

options.label: Walima
options.description: The celebration hosted after the nikah.

options.label: Pheras
options.description: The Hindu wedding rites around the sacred fire.

options.label: Anand Karaj
options.description: The Sikh marriage ceremony centred on the Anand Karaj rites.

options.label: Reception
options.description: The reception celebration with family and friends.

questions.label: Which garment would you like to design?

options.label: Lehenga
options.description: A fitted blouse with a full, flared skirt, usually styled with a dupatta.

options.label: Saree
options.description: A single length of fabric styled through its drape over a fitted blouse — the drape, not stitched construction, defines the look.

options.label: Gharara
options.description: A short kurti with trousers fitted through the upper leg and knee that open into a wide, dramatic flare below the knee.

options.label: Sharara
options.description: A kurti with trousers that flare broadly from the waist or upper leg all the way down.

options.label: Anarkali
options.description: A fitted bodice flowing into a long, frock-style silhouette, usually worn with churidar and dupatta.

options.label: Shalwar kameez
options.description: A kameez worn over shalwar trousers, usually styled with a dupatta.

questions.label: Would you like a particular regional direction?
questions.help_text: Every option can be interpreted many ways; this only sets a general direction.

options.label: A-line
options.description: Skims outward gently from the waist in a clean A - light to wear and universally flattering.

options.label: Full flare
options.description: A circular skirt with maximum sweep - made for twirling and grand entrances.

options.label: Mermaid
options.description: Fitted through the hips and flaring below the knee - modern and sculptural.

options.label: Straight cut
options.description: Falls straight and sleek, often with a slit for movement - quietly contemporary.

options.label: Panelled kali
options.description: Traditional stitched panels (kalis) give heirloom structure and fullness.

options.label: Classic saree
options.description: The timeless free-draped saree - pleats at the front, pallu over the shoulder.

options.label: Lehenga saree
options.description: Pre-pleated to fall like a lehenga skirt - the drama of a saree, none of the draping.

options.label: Pre-stitched
options.description: Sewn into place so you simply step in - effortless for long celebrations.

options.label: Half saree
options.description: The langa-voni: skirt, blouse and a draped voni - a South Indian favourite.

options.label: Classic
options.description: The traditional knee-flare gharara with a short kurti - timeless Lucknowi grace.

options.label: Farshi
options.description: Floor-trailing and voluminous - the grandest, most regal form of the gharara.

options.label: Slim modern
options.description: A pared-back flare with a longer kameez - a contemporary take.

options.label: Classic flare
options.description: Loose from the waist with a generous sweep - the traditional sharara.

options.label: High-waisted
options.description: Fitted at the natural waist before flaring - elongating and modern.

options.label: Farshi
options.description: Extra-long, floor-pooling flare in the old courtly style.

options.label: Floor-length
options.description: The flare falls all the way to the floor - a gown-like sweep.

options.label: Kalidar
options.description: Built from many stitched panels for structured, traditional fullness.

options.label: Front-open
options.description: Opens over a slim inner layer, like a flowing jacket.

options.label: Jacket style
options.description: A longer structured jacket layered over the flare - regal and warm.

options.label: Straight
options.description: A clean, straight-falling kameez - understated and elegant.

options.label: A-line
options.description: Flares softly from the bust for gentle movement.

options.label: Angrakha
options.description: A crossover, wrap-tied bodice in the Mughal court style.

options.label: Long-line
options.description: An ankle-grazing kameez with a stately, columnar fall.

questions.label: The fabric
questions.help_text: The colour the cloth itself is dyed.

questions.label: The embroidery
questions.help_text: The colour the handwork is stitched in.

questions.label: The dupatta
questions.help_text: Match the fabric, or set the dupatta apart in its own colour.

options.label: Match the fabric
options.description: The dupatta takes the same colour as the fabric.

questions.label: Your own colours
questions.help_text: Colours you have added yourself. They stay available across all three choices above.

questions.label: Any fabrics you are drawn to?
questions.help_text: Optional — leave empty to let the concept choose.

options.label: Satin
options.description: A smooth fabric with a lustrous face that catches light cleanly.

questions.label: Which embellishment work speaks to you?
questions.help_text: Pick up to five, or choose "No embellishment" for an unadorned look.

questions.label: How richly worked should it be?
Which neckline would you like?
questions.help_text: Optional — leave this to "No preference" to let the concept choose a neckline that suits the silhouette.

options.label: Classic crew
options.description: A rounded neckline that sits at the base of the neck.

options.label: Curved scoop
options.description: A softly rounded neckline scooped below the collarbone.

options.label: V-neck
options.description: A V-shaped neckline of moderate depth.

options.label: Deep V-neck
options.description: A pronounced V that plunges well below the collarbone.

options.label: Boat neck
options.description: A wide neckline running straight across from shoulder to shoulder.

options.label: Square neck
options.description: A neckline cut in a clean square across the chest.

options.label: Sweetheart
options.description: A curved neckline shaped like the top of a heart.

options.label: High neck
options.description: A neckline that rises high on the neck for fuller coverage.

options.label: Band or mandarin collar
options.description: An upright band or mandarin collar standing at the neck.

options.label: Sleeveless
options.description: No sleeve - shoulders bare, ideal under a heavy dupatta.

options.label: Cap sleeve
options.description: A whisper of a sleeve, just covering the shoulder.

options.label: Elbow
options.description: Ends at the elbow - balanced and comfortable.

options.label: Three-quarter
options.description: Ends mid-forearm, leaving room for bangles and mehndi.

options.label: Full sleeve
options.description: To the wrist - elegant coverage and a canvas for embroidery.

questions.label: How should the back be cut?

options.label: Open back
options.description: A deep open back - dramatic from every angle.

options.label: Deep cut
options.description: A generous scoop, softened with dori ties or latkans.

options.label: Modest
options.description: A high, covered back - comfortable and traditional.

options.label: Bare
options.description: A classic gap between blouse and skirt - traditional for sarees and lehengas.

options.label: Semi-sheer
options.description: Veiled with net or organza - coverage with lightness.

options.label: Covered
options.description: Fully covered by a longer bodice or kameez.

options.label: Uncovered
options.description: Hair dressed and open - the dupatta stays on the shoulders.

options.label: Dupatta over head
options.description: The dupatta drawn gracefully over the head - traditional for many ceremonies.

options.label: Veil style
options.description: A long, trailing veil-style dupatta pinned from the crown.

options.label: Hijab
options.description: Full coverage with the hair completely covered - styled to sit with the outfit.

questions.label: How should the dupatta be styled?

options.label: One shoulder
options.description: Pinned at one shoulder to fall in a single clean cascade.

options.label: Seedha pallu
options.description: Draped across the front from the right shoulder - displays the work fully.

options.label: Over the head
options.description: Framing the face from the crown - soft, bridal and traditional.

options.label: Double dupatta
options.description: One framing the head and shoulders, a second trailing - grand and layered.

options.label: Trail
options.description: Pinned to sweep behind you like a train.

questions.label: How should the saree be draped?
questions.help_text: Drape styles carry their own regional histories — pick the one you love.

options.label: Nivi drape
options.description: Front-tucked pleats with the pallu over the left shoulder - the timeless classic.

options.label: Bengali atpoure
options.description: Broad box pleats with the pallu wrapped around both shoulders.

options.label: Seedha pallu
options.description: The pallu brought over the right shoulder to fan across the front.

options.label: Lehenga drape
options.description: Pleats fanned like a skirt with a fitted wrap - a modern shortcut.

questions.label: Anything else we should know?
questions.help_text: Optional — a short note about anything the questionnaire didn't ask.
